HostFees.title: Platform fee
HostFees.metaDescription: Kvaterka takes 5% from the host after a completed rental. No fees for posting and no commission from the tenant.
HostFees.lede: One fee, one rate, one moment it's charged: {rate}% from the host after the rental ends and both sides confirm it.

highlight.label: from the host — once per rental, only after both sides confirm it happened.

whatsNot.heading: What there isn't
whatsNot.li1: A fee for posting a listing.
whatsNot.li2: A fee for boosting search placement.
whatsNot.li3: A commission from the tenant — they pay only the amount you agreed on.

when.heading: When it's charged
when.p1Rich: The fee is charged once per rental, and only once the rental is marked as completed. A cancelled, expired, or unrealized rental doesn't create a fee.
when.p2: Charging it twice is impossible: three independent database constraints prevent that, not a check in the code. A repeat request returns the same result, not a second charge.

how.heading: How it's calculated
how.p1: The fee is {rate}% of the rental amount for the confirmed term. All amounts are stored in kopecks as whole numbers, and rounding is deterministic, so recalculating a year later gives the same kopeck.
how.p2Rich: The <link>Finance</link> section shows every charge: which rental it's for, what base amount, and at what rate.

debt.heading: Outstanding balance
debt.p1Rich: An unpaid fee limits posting new listings — but it doesn't touch a rental already underway. Evicting a tenant over a host's debt would punish the wrong person.
debt.p2: Fee records are immutable. An error is corrected not by editing the row but with an offsetting entry stating the reason and the author — so the history can be checked, not just read.
debt.noteRich: What isn't ready yet. There's no way to pay a charged fee inside the platform yet: no payment provider is connected. The fee is calculated and recorded, but transferring money through Kvaterka isn't possible right now.
